description: Binance Staked ETH (wBETH) is Binance's custodial liquid staking token. Users deposit ETH into the wBETH contract and Binance forwards it off-chain to its own validators; holders receive wBETH whose exchange rate against ETH ratchets up daily as staking rewards accrue. Aggregate user value is reflected in the wBETH market cap of {{wbethMarketCap}} — on-chain ETH held by the protocol contracts is a small fraction of this since deposited ETH is immediately routed to a Binance-controlled hot wallet (`ethReceiver`). All administrative roles (owner, pauser, blacklister, masterMinter, oracle, operator, proxy admin) are EOAs operated by Binance; there is no DAO, timelock, or community signalling, and contracts are upgradeable at any time without delay.

eth:0xA3eE6926edcce93BacF05F4222c243c4d9.name: Proxy Admin (EOA)
eth:0xA3eE6926edcce93BacF05F4222c243c4d9.description: Binance-controlled EOA holding the proxy `$admin` slot on both wBETH (`WrapTokenV3ETH`) and the unwrap contract (`UnwrapTokenV1ETH`). Can call `changeAdmin`, `upgradeTo`, and `upgradeToAndCall` to swap implementations or rotate the admin slot at any time, with no timelock and no on-chain delay. Worst case = full implementation replacement, capped at the wBETH market cap ({{wbethMarketCap}}) since the new logic could mint unlimited wBETH or block all user exits.

eth:0x099d699C07Bbc8eE6eB5703746063E04B2.name: Operations Owner (EOA)
eth:0x099d699C07Bbc8eE6eB5703746063E04B2.description: Binance-controlled EOA holding the most powerful on-chain role set. Acts as `owner`, `pauser`, `blacklister`, and `masterMinter` on both `WrapTokenV3ETH` and `UnwrapTokenV1ETH`, plus `owner` of `ExchangeRateUpdater`. Can pause transfers/withdrawals, blacklist individual holders, configure minters with arbitrary mint allowance (effectively unlimited mint), rotate every other admin role (`updatePauser`, `updateBlacklister`, `updateMasterMinter`, `updateOracle`, `updateEthReceiver`, `updateOperator`), and replace the exchange-rate oracle contract. Worst-case impact bounded by the wBETH market cap ({{wbethMarketCap}}).

eth:0x2B59215778e99035CF38663454eF1240a7.name: Operator (EOA)
eth:0x2B59215778e99035CF38663454eF1240a7.description: Binance hot key handling day-to-day fund flows. On wBETH it can `supplyEth`, `moveToStakingAddress` (forwards contract ETH to the owner-set `ethReceiver`), and `moveToUnwrapAddress` (system-fixed). On the unwrap contract it can `allocate` pending withdraw requests, `moveToBackAddress` (only the surplus over pending requests, by accounting), `setLockTime` (≥ 2 days, no upper bound — can defer claims indefinitely), and update the `ethStaked` accounting field. On-chain ETH directly under operator control is the contracts' transient ETH balance ({{wbethBalances}} + {{unwrapBalances}}).

eth:0x3E4BD5FB2fCeF981BAFd1D164f838DFC31.name: Recharge Address (EOA)
eth:0x3E4BD5FB2fCeF981BAFd1D164f838DFC31.description: Binance funding wallet. Can call `rechargeFromRechargeAddress` on the unwrap contract to top up withdrawal liquidity (payable-add-only). Cannot extract funds — granting recharge rights to a different EOA via `setRechargeAddress` (owner-only) shifts only the funding-input identity, not extraction rights.

eth:0x0000000000000000000000000000000000.name: Zero Address (Renounced)
eth:0x0000000000000000000000000000000000.description: The `rescuer` field on `WrapTokenV3ETH` is set to address(0), so `rescueERC20` always reverts. The Operations Owner can re-enable it via `updateRescuer` at any time, in which case the rescuer could move any ERC-20 mistakenly held by the contract; in normal operation the wBETH contract holds only ETH, so the practical impact of re-enabling is limited to mistakenly-sent ERC-20s.

eth:0x81720695e43A39C52557Ce6386feB3FAAC.name: ExchangeRateUpdater (Immutable Contract)
eth:0x81720695e43A39C52557Ce6386feB3FAAC.description: Sole permitted caller of `WrapTokenV3ETH.updateExchangeRate`. Itself an immutable contract that enforces a per-caller allowance/interval rate-limit (`configureCaller`) on rate updates. The Operations Owner controls the caller whitelist on this contract, and can also bypass the rate-limit entirely by replacing the oracle pointer via `WrapTokenV3ETH.updateOracle` to point at a fresh contract.

eth:0xa2E3356610840701BDf5611a53974510Ae.name: WrapTokenV3ETH (System Caller)
eth:0xa2E3356610840701BDf5611a53974510Ae.description: The wBETH proxy itself is the only address allowed to call `requestWithdraw` and `moveFromWrapContract` on `UnwrapTokenV1ETH` (gated by an immutable `WBETH_TOKEN_ADDRESS` constant). These are system callbacks invoked when a user calls `requestWithdrawEth`/`moveToUnwrapAddress` on the wrap contract; they create withdraw requests or forward ETH to fund withdrawals and have no extraction path of their own.

eth:0xa2E3356610840701BDf5611a53974510Ae.name: WrapTokenV3ETH (wBETH)
eth:0xa2E3356610840701BDf5611a53974510Ae.description: The wBETH ERC-20 itself. `tokenInfo.tokenValue` reflects the aggregate market cap of {{wbethMarketCap}} held across all wBETH holders — this is the user value at risk from administrative action (mint dilution, transfer pause, blacklist, exchange-rate manipulation). The contract's own ETH balance ({{wbethBalances}}) is transient: deposits flow through to the off-chain `ethReceiver` via `moveToStakingAddress`.

eth:0x79973d557CD9dd87eb61E250cc2572c990.name: UnwrapTokenV1ETH
eth:0x79973d557CD9dd87eb61E250cc2572c990.description: Holds {{unwrapBalances}} in ETH allocated against pending user withdraw requests. Funded by `rechargeFromRechargeAddress` (recharge EOA) and `moveFromWrapContract` (wBETH proxy); paid out by user-initiated `claimWithdraw` after `lockTime` (currently 10 days) elapses.
